title: externalize private data so v2 is safe to publish to public GitHub
author: the operator
trigger: operator directive 2026-09-08: 'after the work is done I wanna be able to upload this to the public GitHub while keeping the environmental files get ignored. And yeah, nothing should point to me or my IP addressing schemes and comments should be sanitized with words like manager or person or other things like that.'
background: v2 already loads camera credentials, the telegram bot token, and the home chat identifier from gitignored env files (camera-creds.env, ~/.env via _load_home_env). What remains for a safe public GitHub push is (a) sanitize prose references in code comments, docstrings, and operator-facing PRD/markdown/HTML docs; (b) replace production /24 IP literals in tests with RFC 5737 documentation prefixes; (c) externalize the operator's home directory paths that the launchd plist generator embeds in its output template; (d) anonymize the operator handle and helper handles that appear in code comments and in data/vehicles/known_vehicles.json verify_notes and the owner field; (e) add a regression guard (scripts/check_no_private_data.py + pre-push hook) so future commits cannot reintroduce these literals; (f) push to a public GitHub repo the operator will provide.
shipping_definition: All ten US-018 stories marked done; pytest 122/122 (or higher) green; tree clean; the canonical pre-push grep across tracked files (the production /24 prefix, the chat identifier digits, operator handle, helper handles) returns zero hits; the public GitHub remote added by the operator exists; first push to public GitHub completed.
scope_exclusions: Secrets (bot token, RTSP credentials) are NOT in this PRD — they already live in gitignored env files (verified 2026-09-08). This PRD only sanitizes prose/code/HTML/tests that previously hard-coded or named private data.
Operator chat handle in the operator's hermes profile is NOT in this PRD — that lives outside the repo.
Helper handle anonymization (US-018e) covers verify_note prose only. The 'owner' field for non-operator-owned vehicles (if any) is left alone; only operator-owned entries get rewritten.
VISION_LLM_URL default 'http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions' is a generic localhost default (low-stakes, no internal IP, no secret); left as-is and noted in PRIVACY.md (US-018i).
design_principles: Anonymize via neutral role-words: 'the operator' (replacing whatever handle appears in code/docs/data); '[helper-A]' (replacing whatever helper handle appears). Reason: matches the operator's literal direction ('manager or person or other things like that') and stays consistent with the existing convention already in infra/quick_classifier.py.

Replace production-prefix literals with the RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 range (192.0.2.0/24). Reason: standard for documentation/test placeholders; reserved-for-documentation per IANA; doesn't collide with any real LAN prefix.
Replace real chat identifier digits with the literal string '<HOME_CHAT_ID>' in prose. Reason: self-documenting placeholder; cannot be mistaken for a real identifier.
Replace literal operator home directory paths with '<PROJECT_ROOT>' / '<HOME_DIR>' in prose. Reason: matches the convention already used in PRD JSONs.
Keep behavioral semantics: anonymization must NOT change runtime behavior. Tests still validate the same logic, just against documentation prefixes.

stories.title: externalize home-directory paths from launchd plist generator template
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** listener/daemon.py contains a function that renders a launchd plist string. The template embeds literal home-directory paths under the operator's username, plus a literal project-root path. These literals identify the operator's machine and would leak the operator's home directory layout if rendered to a committed file. Externalize by reading the username via os.environ.get('USER') (with os.getuid() fallback) and the project root via infra.paths.PROJECT_ROOT (which already exists for exactly this kind of lookup). The rendered plist template must contain zero literal '/Users/<name>/' substrings. **Why medium story:** the function is short but the changes span template rewrite + a new unit test that asserts no literal home path appears in the rendered template. **Depends on nothing:** standalone fix to one file.
ac: AC1: grep '/Users/' over the rendered template output of the plist generator returns zero hits.
AC2: a new pytest in tests/ exists that calls the generator and asserts the rendered string contains only env-resolved paths or placeholder tokens, never a literal username-derived path.
AC3: pytest 122/122 (or higher) green after the change.
AC4: the change is one commit, message 'fix(v2): US-018a — externalize home paths from plist generator template'.
stories.rationale: The only production-code source file that still hard-codes a home-directory username literal. Closes the largest single source-side leak (operator username + project root path) in one shot.

stories.title: replace production camera IPs in tests/test_alert_route.py and tests/test_camera_creds.py with RFC 5737 documentation prefixes
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Both test files use production-prefix IPs as inputs for IP-validation, X-Forwarded-For spoofing, and camera-creds fixture assertions. Replace every literal production-prefix IP in these two test files with an RFC 5737 documentation prefix (192.0.2.X). Preserve the existing test semantics — the new IPs must still be valid IPs that exercise the same code paths (allowlist match, XFF parsing, RTSP-URL composition). **Why small standalone story:** mechanical find-and-replace plus a one-line comment explaining the prefix choice. **Why depends on US-018a:** the test suite should land after the only true source-side leak is closed, so the test changes are test-only and not the bulk of the leak surface.
ac: AC1: grep -nE '<production_prefix>' tests/test_alert_route.py returns zero hits.
AC2: grep -nE '<production_prefix>' tests/test_camera_creds.py returns zero hits.
AC3: pytest 122/122 (or higher) green; the IP-validation test paths still execute (same assertion semantics, different IPs).
AC4: a short comment in each test file explaining the prefix choice, citing RFC 5737.
stories.rationale: Tests must not propagate the operator's network topology. RFC 5737 prefixes are reserved for documentation and cannot collide with a real LAN.

stories.title: sanitize production-prefix example in infra/camera_creds.py docstring
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** infra/camera_creds.py has a docstring example showing the dict shape returned by _parse_env(). The example hard-codes a production-prefix IP as the value for the FRONT entry's 'ip' field, even though no runtime code path uses that literal. Rewrite the example with an RFC 5737 documentation prefix. After this story, the only tracked file containing a production-prefix literal outside of gitignored env files should be camera-creds.env.example's empty values (which are already empty by design). **Why small standalone story:** docstring-only change; trivially verifiable by grep; zero behavioral surface. **Why depends on US-018b:** ordering convention — test fixtures are scrubbed first, then production code's docstrings, so each commit's diff is smaller and reviewable.
ac: AC1: grep -nE '<production_prefix>' infra/camera_creds.py returns zero hits.
AC2: the docstring example still demonstrates _parse_env() return shape correctly.
AC3: pytest 122/122 (or higher) green; no behavioral change.
stories.rationale: Docstring example was a residual from the original author's environment. Replacing it is a one-line edit that closes the last production-prefix leak in production-code source files outside the plist generator (which US-018a handles).

stories.title: sanitize production-prefix IPs and /Users/<name> paths in PRD JSON prose and operator-facing markdown docs
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** The PRD JSONs and V2-LOGIC-FLOW.md contain literal production-prefix IPs and home-directory paths in trigger/background/rationale/AC prose. Replace each literal with a placeholder: production-prefix IPs → '<CAM_<N>_IP>' or '<CAMERA_IP>'; home-directory paths → '<PROJECT_ROOT>' or '<HOME_DIR>'. The PRDs remain semantically complete — they reference the camera IPs as 'a camera IP' rather than 'CAM1's IP at <CAM_1_IP>' — but stop identifying the operator's network or home. **Why medium story:** multi-file prose edit; risk of accidentally rewriting an AC's literal assertion (mitigated by preserving code blocks verbatim). **Why depends on US-018c:** the docs sanitization is the last prose pass after source + tests are scrubbed.
ac: AC1: grep -nE '<production_prefix>' over each of the 5 docs files returns zero hits.
AC2: grep -nE '/Users/[a-z]+/' over each of the 5 docs files returns zero hits.

AC3: spot-check: each PRD still describes its trigger/rationale/AC semantically — re-reading shows the IP replaced by a placeholder, the path replaced by a placeholder, the operational logic unchanged.
AC4: pytest not affected (docs only), but the docs/PRIVACY.md (US-018i) must cite these files as the sanitization contract once US-018i lands.
AC5: one commit per file OR a single combined commit; commit message 'docs(v2): US-018d — sanitize production-prefix IPs and home paths in PRD/markdown prose'.
stories.rationale: Operator-facing prose is what gets screen-shared, blogged about, or quoted in tickets. Even non-public docs should not contain the operator's actual network topology once the repo is GitHub-public.
stories.notes: Original c98b838 missed 3 leaks: RECREATION.md:5 (Mr. V), V2-LOGIC-FLOW.md:313 (Mr. V), RECREATION.md chat-ID. Manual follow-up at e14ff1b fixes them. stories.title: anonymize operator and helper handles in data/vehicles/known_vehicles.json
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** known_vehicles.json contains: (a) ~10 vehicles with the literal 'owner' field set to a personal first-name handle (the operator's); (b) ~7 verify_note entries that name a personal handle (the operator's); (c) 2 verify_note entries that name real third-party helpers. Anonymize: (a) rewrite operator-owned entries' 'owner' field to 'operator' (machine-readable, anonymized); (b) in verify_note prose, replace operator handles with 'the operator' (matching the convention already in infra/quick_classifier.py); (c) replace helper handles with '[helper-A]' / '[helper-B]' generic tags, applied consistently (the same helper always maps to the same tag) so verify_note semantics around disambiguation are preserved. Add a short top-of-file note explaining the anonymization convention. Update tests/test_known_vehicles.py to assert the anonymized values. **Why medium story:** ~20 prose rewrites + 12 'owner' field rewrites + test fixture updates; risk of changing disambiguation semantics if helper tags are assigned inconsistently. **Why depends on US-018d:** prose sanitization is layered — tests, code, PRD docs, then data files.
ac: AC1: scripts/check_no_private_data.py exits 0 when invoked against data/vehicles/known_vehicles.json (the scanner's canonical pattern set covers operator handles; see US-018i for the pattern definitions).

AC2: scripts/check_no_private_data.py exits 0 when invoked against data/vehicles/known_vehicles.json (the scanner's canonical pattern set covers helper handles; see US-018i for the pattern definitions).
AC3: 'owner' field on every vehicle is either 'operator' or another anonymized role (no first names).

AC4: a CONSISTENCY.md-style header comment (or a JSON 'anonymization_note' field) documents the helper tag mapping ([helper-A] = the first helper whose handle appears in the file pre-anonymization, [helper-B] = the second) so future operators can audit, but the actual first names are NOT in the file.
AC5: pytest 122/122 (or higher) green; tests/test_known_vehicles.py assertions updated to match the anonymized values; no test for disambiguation logic removed.
stories.rationale: The largest single-source leak in tracked data files. Operators routinely enroll their own vehicles and helpers' vehicles into this list, so the leak recurs every enrollment — that's exactly the regression class US-018i (PRIVACY.md + scanner) will guard against.

stories.title: scrub operator handle from infra/ code comments (prompt headers + gate/paths/cooldown)
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Six prompt files in infra/ have a header comment naming the operator handle (a personal first-name form like 'Operator-locked contract (<first-name> 2026-09-06):') and three additional source files (gate.py, gate_cooldown.py, paths.py) have inline comments citing a personal handle ('<handle> directive'). Rewrite to 'Operator-locked contract (the operator, 2026-09-06):' and 'operator directive' respectively. Preserve date references (2026-09-06 is a release date, not private). Preserve phase-number references ('Phase 6B.167 §13.4') — those are operational identifiers, not personal. **Why small story:** comment-only edits across 7 files; one-line each. **Why depends on US-018e:** anonymization is layered — data files first (highest signal), then code comments.
ac: AC1: scripts/check_no_private_data.py exits 0 when invoked against infra/ (the scanner's canonical pattern set covers operator handles; see US-018i for the pattern definitions).
AC2: pytest 122/122 (or higher) green; comment edits don't affect behavior.
AC3: spot-check: a sampling of comments retains the phase/release-date references intact.
stories.rationale: Code comments are public by default once on GitHub. Even header docstrings should not name the operator.

stories.title: replace chat identifier digits in PRD/markdown/HTML prose with <HOME_CHAT_ID> placeholder
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Six docs files contain the literal chat identifier digits in prose, table cells, and SVG-style <text> elements (LOGIC-FLOW-DIAGRAM.html). Replace each literal with '<HOME_CHAT_ID>' so the docs still describe the operator's chat but stop identifying the actual identifier. Where the digit literal sits inside a Python string or shell command example that the operator actually runs, leave a TODO note for the operator to replace the placeholder when copying — but DO NOT include the real digits in the committed file. **Why small story:** six files, each with 1-3 occurrences. **Why depends on US-018f:** ordering convention — prose sanitization moves from operator-handle → chat-handle → other handles.
ac: AC1: grep -nE '<chat_identifier_digits>' over each of the 6 docs files returns zero hits.
AC2: grep -nE '<chat_identifier_digits>' over the whole tracked tree (excluding gitignored env files and excluding the canonical scanner pattern in US-018i) returns zero hits.
AC3: visual confirmation: opening LOGIC-FLOW-DIAGRAM.html shows '<HOME_CHAT_ID>' in place of the digit literal in each of its 3 <text> elements; the diagram still renders the same flow.
AC4: pytest not affected (docs only).
stories.rationale: Chat identifier is a long-lived secret that cannot rotate trivially (the operator's phone must re-subscribe). Even one literal leak in a committed file means the identifier is permanently in git history; sanitization is irreversible only by force-pushing or rotating the chat.

stories.title: rename TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID placeholder in telegram-creds.env.example to match the runtime env var name
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** telegram-creds.env.example lists TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID as a placeholder var, but listener/daemon.py reads TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID at runtime. New operators copying the example would set the wrong var name and silently fail to deliver. Rename TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID → TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID in the example. Add a short comment explaining that the var is read from ~/.env via _load_home_env() (US-017b). **Why trivial standalone story:** one-line rename + one comment. **Why depends on nothing:** pure docs fix; doesn't affect runtime or other sanitization.
ac: AC1: grep -nE '^TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=' telegram-creds.env.example returns zero hits.
AC2: grep -nE '^TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID=' telegram-creds.env.example returns one hit.
AC3: a comment near the var explains the runtime read path.
stories.rationale: Pre-existing misnaming risk that would silently break delivery for new operators following the public example file.

stories.title: docs/PRIVACY.md + scripts/check_no_private_data.py + pre-push hook to prevent regression
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Three artifacts together prevent future regressions: (1) docs/PRIVACY.md — short doc describing the convention (what is private, where it lives, what is safe to push, how to spot leaks before commit); (2) scripts/check_no_private_data.py — a grep-based scanner that fails on a production-prefix literal, the chat identifier digits, or operator/helper handle strings in tracked files (excluding gitignored env files and excluding a small whitelist that includes the scanner's own pattern definitions and docs/PRIVACY.md's discussion of what to look for); (3) a .git/hooks/pre-push hook (or a Makefile target invoked by the operator before push) that runs the scanner and blocks the push on a hit. **Why medium-large story:** the scanner itself is small but designing the doc and the whitelist (e.g. allowing the scanner to mention the production-prefix pattern as a thing to grep for) needs care. **Why depends on all others:** the scanner must be tested against a tree that has had all prior stories applied, otherwise it might false-positive on existing leaks.
ac: AC1: docs/PRIVACY.md exists, ≤200 lines, describes the convention and lists the three categories of private data (camera IPs / chat identifier / operator handle), each with the env var or gitignored file it should live in.
AC2: scripts/check_no_private_data.py runs on the current (post-sanitization) tree and exits 0.
AC3: scripts/check_no_private_data.py on a temporary copy of the tree with one faked production-prefix literal injected exits 1 and prints the file:line of the leak.
AC4: a Makefile target (e.g. 'make check-privacy') invokes the scanner, OR a .git/hooks/pre-push hook is installed that invokes the scanner and blocks the push on a non-zero exit.
AC5: pytest 122/122 (or higher) green; one new test under tests/test_check_no_private_data.py asserts both the exit-0 (clean tree) and exit-1 (injected leak) paths.
stories.rationale: Sanitization without a regression guard is a one-time fix. The scanner is the difference between 'safe today' and 'safe forever'.

stories.title: final verification + add public GitHub remote + first push
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Final verification + the actual public GitHub push. After all upstream stories land: (1) run the canonical grep one more time across tracked files (production-prefix literal, chat identifier digits, operator handle, helper handles) — must return zero; (2) run scripts/check_no_private_data.py — must exit 0; (3) add GitHub remote as the operator specifies (the operator provides the GitHub URL; default placeholder is git@github.com:<owner>/farm-surveillance-v2.git); (4) git push github main — first push only, no force, no pull. (5) verify on GitHub that the public repo's tracked files do not contain any of the leak patterns by hitting the GitHub web UI or fetching the tree and grepping. **Operator-driven:** the GitHub owner/repo URL is required and must be provided before this story runs. The operator may also choose to make the repo private initially and flip it to public after a final review.
ac: AC1: canonical grep returns zero across tracked files for all four leak patterns.
AC2: scripts/check_no_private_data.py exits 0.
AC3: GitHub remote added; git remote -v shows both forgejo and github remotes.
AC4: git push github main completes (exit 0) on the first attempt; no force-push; no merge commits.

AC5: verification pass on GitHub: a `git clone` of the GitHub remote into a temp directory, followed by the canonical grep on the freshly cloned tree, returns zero hits. (This proves the push is clean — local-tree-clean ≠ remote-clean if any local hooks fired during push.)
stories.rationale: The user-visible deliverable. Until this story lands, the repo is sanitized but not yet public.
